Our patch_rope.py (agello-litert-lm commit f2e7afa0), in each signature of the sections it patches, looks for CAST ops whose FLOAT32 output name contains maybe_rope/convert_element_type, skips signatures with none and asserts exactly one otherwise; in --split mode it also asserts that the float position has exactly two consumer MULs; it asserts at least one rotary path per section, and handles sections without weights after the graph by repacking the whole flatbuffer.

sources.quote: assert len(casts) == 1, f"{kind}/{sig_name}: expected one rotary CAST, found {len(casts)}"

verifier_note: patch_rope.py at f2e7afa0 L189-193: signatures without a FLOAT32 maybe_rope/convert_element_type CAST are skipped, else assert ==1; the 2-MUL assert (L255) is only in --split mode; non-external sections are repacked whole (L327-329).
original_text: Our patch_rope.py (agello-litert-lm commit f2e7afa0) asserts exactly one rotary CAST (tensor name containing maybe_rope/convert_element_type) and two consumer MULs per signature, and handles sections without external weights by repacking the whole flatbuffer.

text: Google's E2B main graph (b3ca0d2f) stores 2,279,473,152 decoder and output-projection parameters in 776,601,600 bytes of INT2, INT4 and INT8 weights, about 2.7 bits per weight.
verifier_note: e2b-google.json tflite['10'] (tf_lite_prefill_decode): INT2 383,778,816 + INT4 351,535,104 + INT8 41,287,680 = 776,601,600 B. Params 4x+2x+1x = 2,279,473,152; config 3e22461f (35 layers, H 1536, 20 KV-shared double-wide MLP, PLE, per-layer model proj 13,762,560, out proj 402,653,184) gives exactly that. 6,212,812,800/2,279,473,152=2.73.
